tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# BMW Requirements Studio

AI-assisted, evidence-linked **customer requirements for BMW successor vehicles** — built for the BMW
"AI for Product Decision Making" hackathon challenge. The AI ingests BMW customer feedback, customer studies,
sales and option lists, enriches them with cited web research, extracts signals, clusters findings, derives and
scores requirements per derivative × market — and the **product manager decides**, with every step in an
append-only audit trail.

Portfolio-level from day one: 1 Series (F70), 5 Series (G60 + China LWB G68), 7 Series (G70) × EU / US / CN / RoW.

## Quick start

```bash
uv sync                                   # Python 3.12 venv
cp .env.example .env                      # add OPENAI_API_KEY (LLM provider: OpenAI)
uv run python -m api                      # API on http://127.0.0.1:8600 (serves web/dist when built)
cd web && npm install && npm run dev      # PM app (dev) on http://127.0.0.1:5173
cd web && npm run build                   # then the API alone serves the app at http://127.0.0.1:8600
uv run streamlit run app.py               # legacy Streamlit app (being retired, D-039)
```

The raw BMW data (`challange information document/`) and the database (`data/app.db`) are git-ignored.
Demo states (`data/snapshots/`):

| Snapshot | Contents | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `evidence` | all evidence ingested, no requirements | rebuild the pipeline |
| `wave1` | wave 1 done, no PM decisions | **live demo**: review as the PM from scratch |
| `demo` | wave 1 → PM review → wave 2 → PM decides proposals → wave 3 | explore the full ~2-year history |

```bash
uv run python scripts/demo_state.py restore wave1   # stop the app first; keeps the LLM usage log + cache
uv run python scripts/demo_build.py                 # rebuild wave1 + demo from the evidence snapshot
```

## End-to-end workflow

| # | Step | Who | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ingest feedback (10,128 verbatims), customer study, sales, option lists | AI/system, autonomous | `bmw_req.ingest` |
| 2 | Curated reference layer (platforms, plants, competitors, market profiles, brand guardrails) | AI-researched, **PM signs off guardrails** | `bmw_req.reference_data` |
| 3 | Web research agents → cited evidence (URL in search citations, quote verified) | AI, autonomous | `bmw_req.research` |
| 4 | Signal extraction (luna) → findings (embeddings + clustering, per-market/per-wave metrics) | AI, autonomous | `pipeline.extract`, `pipeline.findings` |
| 5 | Requirement derivation (sol), portfolio consolidation, dedup against the existing backlog (merge proposals), evidence linking | AI **proposes** | `pipeline.requirements`, `pipeline.linker` |
| 6 | Fit checks: brand (gate), segment, market, feasibility (context) | AI checks, sol re-checks warn/fail | `pipeline.fit` |
| 7 | Explainable per-target scoring, snapshots, change proposals | AI computes, **PM sets weights** | `pipeline.scoring` |
| 8 | Review: approve / reject / defer / edit / challenge / override gate / confirm priority | **Human, mandatory** | PM app |
| 9 | Audit trail, export | system | PM app → Audit trail / Export |

Repeated per **simulated ingest wave** (LangGraph orchestrator `pipeline.graph`): wave 1 kick-off, wave 2
(+6 months: more feedback, customer study, new sales), wave 3 (+12 months: market event from web research).
Scores are recomputed automatically; priority changes against a PM-confirmed priority become **change
proposals** with their factor-level cause.

## How the deliverables map

| BMW deliverable | Where |
|---|---|
| Concept + working prototype | this repo; PM app: Home → How it works → Review requirements → Priorities by market → AI suggestions (sidebar "Demo tour" walks the path) |
| Structured requirement list (ID, description, findings+sources, score, rationale, evidence level, assumptions/uncertainties, status) | Export page (JSON / CSV / Markdown), `service.export_requirements` |
| Workflow definition: AI autonomous vs mandatory human review | table above; Home ("How it works") and Pipeline & data pages; `foundation/documents/architecture.md` |
| Audit trail: sources → findings → consolidation → scoring → prioritization → human decision | Requirement → Audit tab; Audit trail page; `audit_event` (append-only via triggers) |

## Key design choices

- **Evidence vs assumption** kept apart in every requirement; conflicting evidence linked as `contradicts`.
- **Markets are different customers** — every derivative × market target has its own score, evidence level and
  priority; missing data (e.g. no China verbatims) is shown as an evidence gap, not silently scored as zero.
- **Brand fit** is an approval gate (PM override with rationale); **feasibility** is non-blocking context.
- **$100 OpenAI budget** enforced by a reserving wrapper; every call logged in `llm_usage`, identical calls cached.

Project memory, decisions (D-001 … ) and open questions live in `foundation/`.

# Foundation — start here every session

This folder is the project's memory. Every agent (Claude, Codex, humans) reads it at session start and keeps it current.

## Read order (session start)

1. `STATE.md` — where we are, team, demo path, what's next, budget.
2. `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` — the "Open" section; check if any question blocks your task.
3. `DECISIONS.md` — the **Index** table; open full entries only when relevant (don't re-litigate without new info).
4. Only the `documents/` your task needs (see the table in `AGENTS.md`).

## Write rules (session end / after meaningful work)

- `STATE.md`: update "Current phase", "In progress", "Next up", the Budget table after paid runs, and add one line to the "Session log".
- `DECISIONS.md`: append a new `D-xxx` entry for every decision (who decided, why, alternatives) **and add it to the Index**. Statuses: `accepted` · `proposed` · `superseded by D-xxx`.
- `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`: add new `Q-xxx` entries in numeric order. When answered, move them to "Resolved" with the answer and link the resulting decision.
- `documents/`: keep reference docs true to the code. If you change the stack, schema or workflow, update the doc in the same change. State each fact **once**: other docs link to it instead of copying it.
- Never present something as decided unless a `D-xxx` says so. Changing the stack (D-015–D-020) needs the team.

## Folder map

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `STATE.md` | Live project status, team, demo path, budget, session log |
| `DECISIONS.md` | Append-only decision log (`D-xxx`) with index |
| `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` | Open / resolved questions (`Q-xxx`) |
| `documents/challenge-brief.md` | BMW challenge distilled: mission, scope (+ tensions), deliverables, judging signals, mentor input |
| `documents/data-inventory.md` | Every provided dataset: schema, verified counts, quirks, coverage |
| `documents/tech-stack.md` | Decided stack, budget guard as built, what's still open |
| `documents/architecture.md` | End-to-end workflow, AI vs. human steps, logical data model, audit trail |
| `documents/requirement-model.md` | Requirement schema, evidence levels, gates, prioritization draft |
| `documents/knowledge-base.md` | 3-layer knowledge base, research agents, trust tiers, brand fit & feasibility |
| `documents/portfolio-reference.md` | Platforms, plants, production, BMW sales (cited) |
| `documents/competitor-landscape.md` | Competitors per segment × market, demand trends, brand positioning (cited) |
| `documents/bmw-annual-report-2025.md` | BMW Group Report 2025 extract (T1, page-cited) |
| `documents/glossary.md` | Codes, platforms, data and model terms |

## Fresh clone

1. **Raw data** (not in git): put the BMW challenge folder at the repo root under its original name `challange information document/` (typo intended), containing `mission.md`, `BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf`, the three PNGs and `BMW-Data/` (3 feedback xlsx, customer studies xlsx, `sales_volumes.xlsx`, 3 option-list PDFs). Get it from the team. Treat it as read-only.
2. **Python**: `uv sync` (creates `.venv` with Python 3.12 from `pyproject.toml`). Tests: `uv run pytest`. UI: `uv run python -m api` + `cd web && npm install && npm run dev` (D-039; legacy: `uv run streamlit run app.py`). Don't use the system anaconda Python (broken pandas).
3. **PDF tools**: `brew install poppler` for `pdftotext` (option lists) and `pdftoppm`. The briefing PDF has no text layer, so render it with `pdftoppm` to read it.
4. **Secrets**: copy `.env.example` to `.env`, then add `OPENAI_API_KEY` (ask Atahan).
5. **Derived data** and the SQLite DB go to `data/` (git-ignored).

# Foundation — start here every session

This folder is the project's memory. Every agent (Claude, Codex, humans) reads it at session start and keeps it current.

## Read order (session start)

1. `STATE.md` — where we are, team, demo path, what's next, budget.
2. `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` — the "Open" section; check if any question blocks your task.
3. `DECISIONS.md` — the **Index** table; open full entries only when relevant (don't re-litigate without new info).
4. Only the `documents/` your task needs (see the table in `AGENTS.md`).

## Write rules (session end / after meaningful work)

- `STATE.md`: update "Current phase", "In progress", "Next up", the Budget table after paid runs, and add one line to the "Session log".
- `DECISIONS.md`: append a new `D-xxx` entry for every decision (who decided, why, alternatives) **and add it to the Index**. Statuses: `accepted` · `proposed` · `superseded by D-xxx`.
- `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`: add new `Q-xxx` entries in numeric order. When answered, move them to "Resolved" with the answer and link the resulting decision.
- `documents/`: keep reference docs true to the code. If you change the stack, schema or workflow, update the doc in the same change. State each fact **once**: other docs link to it instead of copying it.
- Never present something as decided unless a `D-xxx` says so. Changing the stack (D-015–D-020) needs the team.

## Folder map

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `STATE.md` | Live project status, team, demo path, budget, session log |
| `DECISIONS.md` | Append-only decision log (`D-xxx`) with index |
| `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` | Open / resolved questions (`Q-xxx`) |
| `documents/challenge-brief.md` | BMW challenge distilled: mission, scope (+ tensions), deliverables, judging signals, mentor input |
| `documents/data-inventory.md` | Every provided dataset: schema, verified counts, quirks, coverage |
| `documents/tech-stack.md` | Decided stack, budget guard as built, what's still open |
| `documents/architecture.md` | End-to-end workflow, AI vs. human steps, logical data model, audit trail |
| `documents/requirement-model.md` | Requirement schema, evidence levels, gates, prioritization draft |
| `documents/knowledge-base.md` | 3-layer knowledge base, research agents, trust tiers, brand fit & feasibility |
| `documents/portfolio-reference.md` | Platforms, plants, production, BMW sales (cited) |
| `documents/competitor-landscape.md` | Competitors per segment × market, demand trends, brand positioning (cited) |
| `documents/bmw-annual-report-2025.md` | BMW Group Report 2025 extract (T1, page-cited) |
| `documents/glossary.md` | Codes, platforms, data and model terms |

## Fresh clone

1. **Raw data** (not in git): put the BMW challenge folder at the repo root under its original name `challange information document/` (typo intended), containing `mission.md`, `BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf`, the three PNGs and `BMW-Data/` (3 feedback xlsx, customer studies xlsx, `sales_volumes.xlsx`, 3 option-list PDFs). Get it from the team. Treat it as read-only.
2. **Python**: `uv sync` (creates `.venv` with Python 3.12 from `pyproject.toml`). Tests: `uv run pytest`. UI: `uv run python -m api` + `cd web && npm install && npm run dev` (D-039; legacy: `uv run streamlit run app.py`). Don't use the system anaconda Python (broken pandas).
3. **PDF tools**: `brew install poppler` for `pdftotext` (option lists) and `pdftoppm`. The briefing PDF has no text layer, so render it with `pdftoppm` to read it.
4. **Secrets**: copy `.env.example` to `.env`, then add `OPENAI_API_KEY` (ask Atahan).
5. **Derived data** and the SQLite DB go to `data/` (git-ignored).

lines: # design review captures contain confidential customer quotes
"reason": "agent triage: L137 .ladder-rail::after is a CSS-triangle arrowhead (transparent borders + 5px border-left) on the ladder scale, not a card side accent"
+Scope: the whole PM web app (`frontend/`), Operate mode, demo-first (live pitch to BMW judges on laptop/projector) but a real tool.
+Audience/job: PM decides what successor cars offer per market; judges watch the process.
+Constraints: dark only, BMW-like blue accent, no BMW logo, English + current domain terms, localhost only.
+Inspiration pinned by user: Fey (web) — calm near-black, dense refined data, floating dock, ⌘K, AI recap card, right drawers.

+THESIS: The PM's decision tool speaks the language of the car it decides about: one cockpit where the car itself is the canvas and every number unfolds to the customer's words. Refuses the sidebar-of-pages admin dashboard and the card-grid of KPI tiles.

+OWN-WORLD: Near-black cabin glass (#08090b → #0e1014 panels, hairline #1d2027), one BMW-blue (#1c69d4 / #4d94ff) for decisions and focus; telltale lights for state (amber conflict, red fail, green approved, dashed blue AI-proposal). Mona Sans: wide/light numerals as instrument readouts, normal width for text. Thin score arcs, band ticks at 45/60, lucide strokes.
+STORY: See what changed since last wave → decide in one queue with reasons → see the result on the car per market → open any number down to quotes → prove it in the audit timeline.

+FIRST VIEWPORT: Panoramic status band (product, SIMULATION wave 3 · Nov 2027 with wave ticks, actor, spend, ⌘K). Briefing: left 7/12 AI-free wave briefing paragraph with inline delta chips and "N decisions waiting" primary action; right 5/12 portfolio pulse (car × market grid, Must counts, evidence gaps). Below: "Since last wave" event feed. Floating dock bottom centre.
+FORM: cockpit HMI × Fey restraint — own list position 3; seed key 3c8f88bb.
+SIGNATURE: car zone focus — camera flies to a zone, body turns x-ray for interior zones, the requirement list scrolls in sync; rotary J/K stepping in the decision queue.
+FINISH: unreviewed and undocumented is unfinished; this build ends with the finish review, the verdict, DESIGN.md, and every shipping raster carrying its provenance

+Mode: Operate. Audience: the BMW PM (Atahan) and hackathon judges on a laptop/projector. Job: see every piece of raw evidence the system holds, as one space, at a checkpoint; switch Jan 26 → Jul 26 and see what the second sweep added. Constraints: localhost only (confidential comments), black only, near-textless, 3D-first; checkpoint 2 always builds on checkpoint 1 (tracks, not snapshots).
+THESIS: each checkpoint is a radar sweep over one fixed evidence space; the app shows what a sweep acquired and how every track changed. Refuses the sidebar-plus-chart-cards dashboard.

+OWN-WORLD: true black scan volume, white contacts, one BMW blue for the sweep and PM marks, amber only for weakened/lost; hairline range rings; mark shape encodes state (ring new, dot held, double ring strengthened, cross lost); numerals are the main text, wide Mona Sans.
+STORY: the PM sees all raw evidence as one space, sweeps to July, watches new contacts flare in, hovers one to read the customer's words, filters by car or market.

+FIRST VIEWPORT: full-bleed 3D galaxy of ~10k comments in a slowly turning scan volume; top-left three readout numerals; bottom-right the JAN 26 / JUL 26 sweep control; left edge a thin car/market key; click opens a right-side sheet with the comment.
+FORM: own list candidate 5 of 7, track-while-scan; seed 8f8f8a79. Signature interaction: switching checkpoint sends a sweep plane through the volume, contacts it passes light up.
+FINISH: unreviewed and undocumented is unfinished; this build ends with the finish review, the verdict, DESIGN.md, and every shipping raster carrying its provenance
+## Recorded adaptations (2026-10-11, after the first finish review)

+- User-pinned: each raw data type has its own colour (comments blue, research orange, study aqua, options yellow, sales magenta; validated categorical palette on black). This replaces "white contacts"; track state stays in mark shape (dot = held, ring = acquired by this sweep), flare and hover go white, the lock reticle is white.
+- User-pinned: no auto-rotation; the volume moves only when the PM drags it. The sweep plays once on arrival (JAN → JUL) when no checkpoint is in the URL.
+- Strengthened / weakened / lost marks and amber do not apply to raw sources (they are only ever acquired); they appear from the clustering stage on, where `track` states change.
+- Key keeps five dimensions (car, market, channel, BMW label, engine): the raw comments carry all five and the PM asked to see the raw data.
+- Every ring element opens an inspector that names its layer and says in one line what the ring encodes (user request).

.PHONY: install api dev build test typecheck

	cd backend && uv sync
	cd frontend && npm install

api:  ## API on http://127.0.0.1:8600 (serves frontend/dist when built)
	cd backend && uv run python -m api

dev:  ## PM app dev server on http://127.0.0.1:5173 (needs `make api`)

EOF

import pathlib,re

]

content.text:
They show the same thing because it's the same app. Both run the code in `frontend/src`; they just deliver it differently.

| | **http://127.0.0.1:8600** | **http://127.0.0.1:5173** |
|---|---|---|
| Who serves the page | The Python API (FastAPI) | Vite, the Node development server |
| What it serves | The built copy in `frontend/dist` (`make build`) | The source files in `frontend/src`, compiled as the browser asks for them |
| When you edit frontend code | Nothing changes until you run `make build` again | The page updates within about a second |
| Where the data comes from | Its own `/api` | It forwards `/api` calls to port 8600 |
| Speed | Faster (minified, a few bundled files) | Slower first load (many unbundled modules) |
| What it needs | Only Python | Node and `npm`, plus the API running |

Right now they match exactly because I ran `make build` during the restructure, so the built copy is up to date with the source. As soon as someone edits a file in `frontend/src`, 5173 shows the change and 8600 keeps showing the old build.

Data and actions are shared: 5173 has no backend of its own, so a decision you make in either tab shows up in the other.

**Which to use:**
- **While changing the frontend:** use 5173.
- **For the demo or pitch:** use 8600. It's one process, faster and won't change mid-presentation. Run `make build` first so it has the latest code.

If you're not editing frontend code right now, you only need 8600, and I can stop the dev server.

content.text:
Yes. The key point is that the frontend doesn't actually run on a server. It runs in your browser.

`make build` turns the React code into a few plain files: one HTML page, some JavaScript and some CSS, all in `frontend/dist`. A server only has to hand those files to the browser once. After that, the browser runs the app and sends requests back to the server for data.

So the Python server on port 8600 does two jobs:

1. **Hands out the app files.** When you open `http://127.0.0.1:8600/`, it sends back `frontend/dist/index.html` and the JavaScript that comes with it.
2. **Answers data requests.** When the app in your browser asks for `/api/...` (for example the requirements or the audit trail), it returns data from the database.

That's set up in `backend/src/api/routers/static.py`: every `/api/...` path goes to the data endpoints, and any other path gets the built files.

Vite on port 5173 only replaces job 1. Instead of handing out the frozen built files, it compiles `frontend/src` on the fly so your edits appear immediately. It can't do job 2, so it forwards every `/api/...` request to port 8600. That's why the API has to run either way, and Vite is only an extra for frontend development.

```
Normal use:   browser ──► :8600  (app files + data)

Frontend dev: browser ──► :5173  (live app files)
                            └── /api/... ──► :8600  (data)
```

from __future__ import annotations
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI
from api.deps import DB

        app.include_router(r)
    app.include_router(STATIC_ROUTER)   # /models + SPA catch-all, must stay last
    return app
app = create_app()
def run() -> None:
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run("api.main:app", host=HOST, port=PORT, log_level="info")
if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()

Localhost only (127.0.0.1:8600), no CORS: the frontend is served from the same origin (frontend/dist) or proxied by the
Vite dev server. Run with `uv run python -m api` or `uv run successor`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI

from api.deps import DB
from api.routers import ROUTERS, STATIC_ROUTER

HOST = "127.0.0.1"   # never 0.0.0.0: the data is BMW-confidential (AGENTS rule 1)
PORT = 8600


@asynccontextmanager
async def _lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    yield
    DB.close()


def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    app = FastAPI(title="Successor — PM decision API", version="1.0", lifespan=_lifespan,
                  docs_url="/api/docs", openapi_url="/api/openapi.json", redoc_url=None)
    for r in ROUTERS:
        app.include_router(r)
    app.include_router(STATIC_ROUTER)   # /models + SPA catch-all, must stay last
    return app


app = create_app()


def run() -> None:
    import uvicorn

    uvicorn.run("api.main:app", host=HOST, port=PORT, log_level="info")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# SharkSight images (D-053). Build context = repo root; .dockerignore is an allowlist (no raw data, data/ or .env).
#   target prod (default): API + built PM app in one container, APP_ENV=production
#   target dev:            API with auto-reload; source is bind-mounted by compose.yaml (profile dev)
# The layout mirrors the repo (/app/backend, /app/frontend, /app/research) so bmw_req.config.ROOT resolves to /app.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- frontend build
FROM node:22-slim AS web
WORKDIR /app/frontend
COPY frontend/package.json frontend/package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY frontend/ ./
RUN npm run build

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- python base
FROM python:3.12-slim AS base
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.5 /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/opt/venv PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
WORKDIR /app/backend
COPY backend/pyproject.toml backend/uv.lock ./
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project
COPY backend/src ./src
COPY backend/scripts ./scripts
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev
COPY research/checkpoints/checkpoints.json /app/research/checkpoints/checkpoints.json
# inside the container the server must listen on all interfaces; compose publishes it on the host's 127.0.0.1 only
ENV API_HOST=0.0.0.0 API_PORT=8600 DATA_DIR=/app/data
EXPOSE 8600
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=20s --retries=3 \
    CMD python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8600/api/state', timeout=4)"
CMD ["python", "-m", "api"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- dev: + pytest, reload
FROM base AS dev
RUN uv sync --frozen
ENV APP_ENV=development

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- prod (default)
FROM base AS prod
COPY --from=web /app/frontend/dist /app/frontend/dist
ENV APP_ENV=production

# SharkSight in containers (D-053). Pick a profile:
#   docker compose --profile prod up -d --build   → http://127.0.0.1:8600 (one container, built app)
#   docker compose --profile dev up --build       → http://127.0.0.1:5173 (Vite, live reload) + API on :8600
# Ports are published on 127.0.0.1 only (AGENTS rule 1). data/ (DB, snapshots, 3D models) is mounted, never baked in.
# Don't run the native API (`make api`) at the same time: same port and same SQLite file.
name: sharksight

x-api: &api
  env_file:
    - path: .env
      required: false
  ports:
    - "127.0.0.1:8600:8600"

services:
  app:
    <<: *api
    profiles: [prod]
    build: { context: ., target: prod }
    image: sharksight:prod
    volumes:
      - ./data:/app/data
    restart: unless-stopped

  api-dev:
    <<: *api
    profiles: [dev]
    build: { context: ., target: dev }
    image: sharksight:dev
    environment:
      APP_ENV: development
    volumes:
      - ./data:/app/data
      - ./backend/src:/app/backend/src
      - ./backend/scripts:/app/backend/scripts
      - ./research:/app/research:ro

  web-dev:
    profiles: [dev]
    image: node:22-slim
    working_dir: /app/frontend
    command: sh -c "npm ci && npx vite --strictPort"
    environment:
      API_URL: http://api-dev:8600
      VITE_HOST: 0.0.0.0
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5173:5173"
    volumes:
      - ./frontend:/app/frontend
      - /app/frontend/node_modules   # container's own (Linux) node_modules, not the host's macOS ones
    depends_on:
      api-dev: { condition: service_healthy }

#   docker compose --profile dev up --build       → http://127.0.0.1:5173 (Vite, live reload) + API on :8600
# Ports are published on 127.0.0.1 only (AGENTS rule 1). data/ (DB, snapshots, 3D models) is mounted, never baked in.
# Don't run the native API (`make api`) at the same time: same port and same SQLite file.
name: sharksight

x-api: &api
  env_file:
    - path: .env
      required: false
  ports:
    - "127.0.0.1:8600:8600"

services:
  app:
    <<: *api
    profiles: [prod]
    build: { context: ., target: prod }
    image: sharksight:prod
    volumes:
      - ./data:/app/data
    restart: unless-stopped

  api-dev:
    <<: *api
    profiles: [dev]
    build: { context: ., target: dev }
    image: sharksight:dev
    environment:
      APP_ENV: development
    volumes:
      - ./data:/app/data
      - ./backend/src:/app/backend/src
      - ./backend/scripts:/app/backend/scripts
      - ./research:/app/research:ro

  web-dev:
    profiles: [dev]
    image: node:22-slim
    working_dir: /app/frontend
    command: sh -c "npm ci && npx vite --strictPort"
    environment:
      API_URL: http://api-dev:8600
      VITE_HOST: 0.0.0.0
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5173:5173"
    volumes:
      - ./frontend:/app/frontend
      - /app/frontend/node_modules   # container's own (Linux) node_modules, not the host's macOS ones
    depends_on:
      api-dev: { condition: service_healthy }

# Common commands from the repo root. Python runs in backend/ (uv), the PM app in frontend/ (npm).

	docker compose --profile dev up --build

message.content: does python code also update itself?

content.text:
Yes in the development profile, no in production. Python updates a bit differently from the frontend.

**Development (`make api` or `make up-dev`)**
The server watches `backend/src`. When you save a `.py` file it restarts itself, which takes a second or two, and the app's next data request gets the new code. I tested this in the dev container earlier: touching `backend/src/api/labels.py` triggered "Reloading..." and the API came back with 200.

The difference from the frontend:
- **Frontend (Vite):** swaps the changed code into the open browser page. The page keeps its state and you see the change immediately.
- **Python:** restarts the whole server process. The browser page stays open, but anything running inside the server is dropped, which is the caveat about AI jobs mentioned before. You may need to reload the page if a view looks stale.

**Production (`make serve` or `make up`)**
Nothing updates on its own:
- `make serve`: stop it and start it again.
- `make up`: the code is copied into the image when it's built, so run `make up` again to rebuild. That's the case for the container running right now.

**Two other cases**
- **Pipeline commands** (`uv run python -m bmw_req…`) and the scripts in `backend/scripts/` start a fresh process each time, so they always use the latest code.
- **New Python packages** (a change to `pyproject.toml`): auto-reload doesn't install them. Run `uv sync` in `backend/`, or `make up-dev` / `make up` for containers, which rebuild the image.

content.text:
**Database:** it's still SQLite, and it's the same file. The production container doesn't get its own database. It mounts `data/app.db` from your disk, the same file that development and the pipeline commands use. "Production" here only changes how the app runs: no auto-restart, and one server hands out the built app. A decision made in the prod container lands in the same database your dev setup reads.

SQLite itself is fine for this app. It's one server process with one PM at a time, and background jobs run as threads inside that process. Swapping to Postgres or similar would only pay off with several server instances or many simultaneous users, and changing the database would also reverse D-016, which needs the team.

**Can it run on a real production server?** Technically yes, since the image is ready. But three things block it as the code stands:

1. **No login.** The app takes the PM's name from a request header and never checks it (`backend/src/api/deps.py:67`). Anyone who can reach the URL can approve or reject requirements as any name. They can also start AI jobs that spend the $100 OpenAI budget.
2. **Confidential data.** The database holds BMW customer verbatims. Rule 1 says that data goes nowhere except OpenAI, so putting it on a cloud server needs BMW's and the team's approval first.
3. **The server holds state.** It needs exactly one instance and a persistent disk for `data/`, so no auto-scaling and no throwaway containers.

**What I'd suggest instead:**
- **Give production its own database.** A small change: the prod container uses its own folder, e.g. `data-prod/`, seeded from the `demo` snapshot. Then dev experiments can't touch the demo state, and the demo can be reset at any time.
- **If BMW judges need to reach it remotely:** keep it on your laptop, put a login in front of it, and share it through a private tunnel rather than a public server.

Should I set up the separate production database? If you do want a real server, tell me where (which cloud, who should have access) and I'll check the confidentiality question with you first.

"""Budget guard (D-014): reserve worst-case cost before a call, settle with actual usage after.

Thresholds are on total committed spend = settled cost + open reservations.
"""

import logging
import sqlite3

from bmw_req.llm.pricing import (
    CACHE_WRITE_FACTOR,
    FLEX_FACTOR,
    PRICES,
    WEB_SEARCH_CONTENT_TOKENS,
    WEB_SEARCH_PER_CALL,
    Price,
)

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

WARN_USD = 45.0
BLOCK_NON_DEMO_USD = 70.0
HARD_STOP_USD = 90.0


class BudgetExceeded(RuntimeError):
    pass


def price_for(model: str) -> Price:
    try:
        return PRICES[model]
    except KeyError:
        raise BudgetExceeded(f"No price for model {model!r}; add it to pricing.py before using it") from None


def estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    """Deliberately high input-token estimate: UTF-8 bytes / 2."""
    return len(text.encode("utf-8")) // 2 + 1


def worst_case_usd(model: str, input_tokens: int, max_output_tokens: int = 0, max_tool_calls: int = 0) -> float:
    """List price (no Flex discount, no cache), plus search calls and their content tokens."""
    p = price_for(model)
    tokens_in = input_tokens + max_tool_calls * WEB_SEARCH_CONTENT_TOKENS
    return (tokens_in * p.input + max_output_tokens * p.output) / 1e6 + max_tool_calls * WEB_SEARCH_PER_CALL


def actual_usd(
    model: str,
    *,
    input_tokens: int,
    cached_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_write_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
    search_calls: int = 0,
    flex: bool = False,
) -> float:
    p = price_for(model)
    uncached = max(input_tokens - cached_tokens - cache_write_tokens, 0)
    tokens_usd = (
        uncached * p.input
        + cached_tokens * p.cached_input
        + cache_write_tokens * p.input * CACHE_WRITE_FACTOR
        + output_tokens * p.output
    ) / 1e6
    if flex:
        tokens_usd *= FLEX_FACTOR
    return tokens_usd + search_calls * WEB_SEARCH_PER_CALL


def spent_usd(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> float:
    return conn.execute("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd), 0) FROM llm_usage WHERE status != 'reserved'").fetchone()[0]


def committed_usd(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> float:
    return conn.execute(
        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'reserved' THEN reserved_usd ELSE cost_usd END), 0) FROM llm_usage"
    ).fetchone()[0]


def reserve(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, job: str, kind: str, model: str, reserved_usd: float, demo: bool) -> int:
    """Insert a reservation row, or raise BudgetExceeded if it would cross a threshold."""
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        after = committed_usd(conn) + reserved_usd
        if after > HARD_STOP_USD:
            raise BudgetExceeded(f"Hard stop: ${after:.2f} would exceed ${HARD_STOP_USD:.0f} ({job})")
        if not demo and after > BLOCK_NON_DEMO_USD:
            raise BudgetExceeded(f"Non-demo jobs blocked: ${after:.2f} would exceed ${BLOCK_NON_DEMO_USD:.0f} ({job})")
        cur = conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO llm_usage (job, demo, kind, model, status, reserved_usd) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'reserved', ?)",
            (job, int(demo), kind, model, reserved_usd),
        )
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    if after > WARN_USD:
        log.warning("LLM spend warning: committed $%.2f > $%.0f — re-estimate the plan (D-014)", after, WARN_USD)
    return cur.lastrowid


def settle(conn: sqlite3.Connection, usage_id: int, *, status: str, cost_usd: float, **fields) -> None:
    """Replace a reservation with actual usage. `fields` are llm_usage columns (tokens, response_id, error, ...)."""
    cols = ["status", "cost_usd", *fields]
    sets = ", ".join(f"{c} = ?" for c in cols)
    conn.execute(
        f"UPDATE llm_usage SET {sets}, settled_at = strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now') WHERE id = ?",
        (status, cost_usd, *fields.values(), usage_id),
    )

"""Budget guard (D-014): reserve worst-case cost before a call, settle with actual usage after.

Thresholds are on total committed spend = settled cost + open reservations.
"""

import logging
import sqlite3

from bmw_req.llm.pricing import (
    CACHE_WRITE_FACTOR,
    FLEX_FACTOR,
    PRICES,
    WEB_SEARCH_CONTENT_TOKENS,
    WEB_SEARCH_PER_CALL,
    Price,
)

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

WARN_USD = 45.0
BLOCK_NON_DEMO_USD = 70.0
HARD_STOP_USD = 90.0


class BudgetExceeded(RuntimeError):
    pass


def price_for(model: str) -> Price:
    try:
        return PRICES[model]
    except KeyError:
        raise BudgetExceeded(f"No price for model {model!r}; add it to pricing.py before using it") from None


def estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    """Deliberately high input-token estimate: UTF-8 bytes / 2."""
    return len(text.encode("utf-8")) // 2 + 1


def worst_case_usd(model: str, input_tokens: int, max_output_tokens: int = 0, max_tool_calls: int = 0) -> float:
    """List price (no Flex discount, no cache), plus search calls and their content tokens."""
    p = price_for(model)
    tokens_in = input_tokens + max_tool_calls * WEB_SEARCH_CONTENT_TOKENS
    return (tokens_in * p.input + max_output_tokens * p.output) / 1e6 + max_tool_calls * WEB_SEARCH_PER_CALL


def actual_usd(
    model: str,
    *,
    input_tokens: int,
    cached_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_write_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
    search_calls: int = 0,
    flex: bool = False,
) -> float:
    p = price_for(model)
    uncached = max(input_tokens - cached_tokens - cache_write_tokens, 0)
    tokens_usd = (
        uncached * p.input
        + cached_tokens * p.cached_input
        + cache_write_tokens * p.input * CACHE_WRITE_FACTOR
        + output_tokens * p.output
    ) / 1e6
    if flex:
        tokens_usd *= FLEX_FACTOR
    return tokens_usd + search_calls * WEB_SEARCH_PER_CALL


def spent_usd(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> float:
    return conn.execute("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd), 0) FROM llm_usage WHERE status != 'reserved'").fetchone()[0]


def committed_usd(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> float:
    return conn.execute(
        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'reserved' THEN reserved_usd ELSE cost_usd END), 0) FROM llm_usage"
    ).fetchone()[0]


def reserve(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, job: str, kind: str, model: str, reserved_usd: float, demo: bool) -> int:
    """Insert a reservation row, or raise BudgetExceeded if it would cross a threshold."""
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        after = committed_usd(conn) + reserved_usd
        if after > HARD_STOP_USD:
            raise BudgetExceeded(f"Hard stop: ${after:.2f} would exceed ${HARD_STOP_USD:.0f} ({job})")
        if not demo and after > BLOCK_NON_DEMO_USD:
            raise BudgetExceeded(f"Non-demo jobs blocked: ${after:.2f} would exceed ${BLOCK_NON_DEMO_USD:.0f} ({job})")
        cur = conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO llm_usage (job, demo, kind, model, status, reserved_usd) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'reserved', ?)",
            (job, int(demo), kind, model, reserved_usd),
        )
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    if after > WARN_USD:
        log.warning("LLM spend warning: committed $%.2f > $%.0f — re-estimate the plan (D-014)", after, WARN_USD)
    return cur.lastrowid


def settle(conn: sqlite3.Connection, usage_id: int, *, status: str, cost_usd: float, **fields) -> None:
    """Replace a reservation with actual usage. `fields` are llm_usage columns (tokens, response_id, error, ...)."""
    cols = ["status", "cost_usd", *fields]
    sets = ", ".join(f"{c} = ?" for c in cols)
    conn.execute(
        f"UPDATE llm_usage SET {sets}, settled_at = strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now') WHERE id = ?",
        (status, cost_usd, *fields.values(), usage_id),
    )

"""In-memory background jobs for the two long, paid pipeline actions: opening a wave and a PM challenge.

One job at a time (both spend OpenAI budget and write a lot). Each job runs in its own thread with its OWN SQLite
connection — the pipeline opens its own anyway — so the shared API connection stays free for reads. Log lines from the
pipeline's return value and from `bmw_req` loggers are captured into the job record.

The pipeline functions are looked up on their modules at call time (`graph.advance`, `challenge.challenge`,
`make_llm`) so tests can monkeypatch them — tests must never trigger a paid call.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import logging
import threading
import traceback
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, Callable

_LOCK = threading.Lock()
_JOBS: dict[str, dict] = {}
_IDS = itertools.count(1)
MAX_KEEP = 50


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f")[:-3] + "Z"


class _Capture(logging.Handler):
    def __init__(self, job: dict):
        super().__init__(level=logging.INFO)
        self.job = job

    def emit(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> None:
        try:
            self.job["log"].append(f"{record.levelname.lower()}: {record.getMessage()}")
        except Exception:
            pass


def running() -> dict | None:
    with _LOCK:
        for j in _JOBS.values():
            if j["status"] == "running":
                return {"id": j["id"], "kind": j["kind"]}
    return None


def get(job_id: str) -> dict | None:
    with _LOCK:
        j = _JOBS.get(job_id)
        return None if j is None else {**j, "log": list(j["log"])}


def start(kind: str, fn: Callable[[Callable[[str], None]], Any], meta: dict | None = None) -> str | None:
    """Start `fn(log)` in a background thread. Returns the job id, or None when another job is running."""
    with _LOCK:
        if any(j["status"] == "running" for j in _JOBS.values()):
            return None
        jid = f"{kind}-{next(_IDS)}"
        job = {"id": jid, "kind": kind, "status": "running", "started_at": _now(), "finished_at": None,
               "log": [], "error": None, "result": None, "meta": meta or {}}
        _JOBS[jid] = job
        if len(_JOBS) > MAX_KEEP:
            for old in [k for k, v in _JOBS.items() if v["status"] != "running"][: len(_JOBS) - MAX_KEEP]:
                _JOBS.pop(old, None)

    def log(line: str) -> None:
        job["log"].append(str(line))

    def target() -> None:
        handler = _Capture(job)
        logger = logging.getLogger("bmw_req")
        logger.addHandler(handler)
        prev_level = logger.level
        if logger.level == logging.NOTSET or logger.level > logging.INFO:
            logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
        try:
            result = fn(log)
            with _LOCK:
                job["result"] = result
                job["status"] = "done"
        except Exception as e:   # surface the failure in the job record
            with _LOCK:
                job["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
                job["status"] = "error"
            job["log"].append("".join(traceback.format_exception_only(type(e), e)).strip())
        finally:
            logger.removeHandler(handler)
            logger.setLevel(prev_level)
            job["finished_at"] = _now()

    threading.Thread(target=target, name=f"job-{jid}", daemon=True).start()
    return jid


def wait(job_id: str, timeout: float = 10.0) -> dict | None:
    """Test helper: block until the job finishes (or timeout)."""
    import time

    end = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while time.monotonic() < end:
        j = get(job_id)
        if j is None or j["status"] != "running":
            return j
        time.sleep(0.02)
    return get(job_id)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ runners
def make_llm(conn):
    """Budget-guarded OpenAI wrapper on the job's own connection (patched in tests)."""
    from bmw_req.llm import LLM

    return LLM(conn=conn)


def run_wave(wave: int, actor: str) -> Callable[[Callable[[str], None]], dict]:
    def fn(log: Callable[[str], None]) -> dict:
        from bmw_req.pipeline import graph

        log(f"opening wave {wave} as {actor} (LLM calls are budget-guarded; replays hit the cache)")
        out = graph.advance(wave, initiated_by=actor)
        for line in out.get("log") or []:
            log(line)
        return {"wave": out.get("wave", wave), "new_requirements": list(out.get("new_requirements") or []),
                "run_id": out.get("run_id")}
    return fn


def run_challenge(req_id: str, question: str, actor: str) -> Callable[[Callable[[str], None]], dict]:
    def fn(log: Callable[[str], None]) -> dict:
        from bmw_req.db import connect
        from bmw_req.pipeline import challenge

        conn = connect()
        try:
            log(f"challenge on {req_id} by {actor}: asking the reasoning model (status → challenged)")
            out = challenge.challenge(conn, make_llm(conn), req_id, question, actor)
            log(f"answered: verdict {(out.get('answer') or {}).get('verdict')}, "
                f"cost ${float(out.get('cost') or 0):.4f}{' (cached)' if out.get('cached') else ''}")
            return out
        finally:
            conn.close()
    return fn

"""Budget guard tests with a fake OpenAI client — no paid calls."""

from types import SimpleNamespace as NS

import httpx
import openai
import pytest

from bmw_req.db import connect
from bmw_req.llm import LLM, BudgetExceeded, budget


def fake_response(input_tokens=1000, cached=0, cache_write=0, output=200, reasoning=50, tier="default", searches=0):
    return NS(
        id="resp_test",
        status="completed",
        model="gpt-6-luna",
        service_tier=tier,
        output_text="ok",
        output=[NS(type="web_search_call")] * searches + [NS(type="message")],
        usage=NS(
            input_tokens=input_tokens,
            input_tokens_details=NS(cached_tokens=cached, cache_write_tokens=cache_write),
            output_tokens=output,
            output_tokens_details=NS(reasoning_tokens=reasoning),
        ),
    )


class FakeResponses:
    def __init__(self, result):
        self.result = result
        self.calls = []

    def create(self, **params):
        self.calls.append(params)
        if isinstance(self.result, Exception):
            raise self.result
        return self.result

    parse = create


@pytest.fixture
def conn():
    return connect(":memory:")


def make_llm(conn, result=None):
    client = NS(responses=FakeResponses(result or fake_response()))
    return LLM(conn=conn, client=client)


def preload(conn, usd, status="completed"):
    conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO llm_usage (job, kind, model, status, reserved_usd, cost_usd) VALUES ('seed', 'responses', 'gpt-6-luna', ?, ?, ?)",
        (status, usd, usd),
    )


def test_actual_cost_standard():
    # 800 uncached + 200 cached input, 200 output on luna
    usd = budget.actual_usd("gpt-6-luna", input_tokens=1000, cached_tokens=200, output_tokens=200)
    assert usd == pytest.approx((800 * 0.10 + 200 * 0.01 + 200 * 0.50) / 1e6)


def test_actual_cost_flex_cache_write_and_search():
    usd = budget.actual_usd(
        "gpt-6.1-sol", input_tokens=2000, cache_write_tokens=1000, output_tokens=100, search_calls=2, flex=True
    )
    tokens = (1000 * 2.00 + 1000 * 2.00 * 1.25 + 100 * 10.00) / 1e6 * 0.5
    assert usd == pytest.approx(tokens + 2 * 0.01)


def test_unknown_model_refused():

        budget.worst_case_usd("gpt-6-astra", 100, 100)

        (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, field,
         None if old is None else (old if isinstance(old, str) else json.dumps(old, ensure_ascii=False)),
         None if new is None else (new if isinstance(new, str) else json.dumps(new, ensure_ascii=False)),
         rationale, model, prompt_ref, run_id),
    )

DB = Database()


@contextmanager
def db() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:

    with LOCK:
        yield DB.conn()


def get_actor(x_actor: str | None = Header(default=None), as_actor: str | None = Query(default=None)) -> str:
    """Named human actor for writes and access events (no auth; header may be percent-encoded for non-Latin-1 names).

    return name or DEFAULT_PM


@contextmanager

    try:

    except ActionError as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=str(e)) from e


def conflict(msg: str) -> HTTPException:
    return HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=msg)


def not_found(msg: str) -> HTTPException:
    return HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=msg)


def need_rationale(rationale: str | None, what: str = "A rationale") -> str:

content.text:
# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__find
entries.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages
entries.description: Read browser console messages (console.log, console.error, console.warn, etc.) from a specific tab. Useful for debugging JavaScript errors, viewing application logs, or understanding what's happening in the browser console. Returns console messages from the current domain only. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs. IMPORTANT: Always provide a pattern to filter messages - without a pattern, you may get too many irrelevant messages.

tabId.description: Tab ID to read console messages from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

onlyErrors.description: If true, only return error and exception messages. Default is false (return all message types).

clear.description: If true, clear the console messages after reading to avoid duplicates on subsequent calls. Default is false.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to filter console messages. Only messages matching this pattern will be returned (e.g., 'error|warning' to find errors and warnings, 'MyApp' to filter app-specific logs). You should always provide a pattern to avoid getting too many irrelevant messages.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 100. Increase only if you need more results.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
entries.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

content.content:
## Budget guard (as built)

- `bmw_req.llm.LLM.generate()` / `.embed()` are the only way to call OpenAI.
- Each call reserves its worst case in `llm_usage` first (input ≈ UTF-8 bytes ÷ 2, + `max_output_tokens`, + `max_tool_calls` × ($0.01 + 20k content tokens)), at list price. Thresholds apply to settled cost + open reservations.
- After the call, the row is settled with actual tokens (cached, cache-write, reasoning), search calls and cost. Flex is discounted only if the response confirms `service_tier == "flex"`.
- API/connection errors settle at $0; any other failure after the request (e.g. parse error) keeps the worst case.
- A crashed process leaves a `reserved` row that keeps counting — settle or delete it by hand.
- Identical requests (same model, prompt, schema, params) are served from `llm_cache` at $0; pass `use_cache=False` to force a new call.
- The Process → System screen (and `GET /api/budget`) shows spend, committed and the usage log.

You can now set the budget and the API key yourself in the app, under **Audit → Usage**. 132 tests pass, including 10 new ones for this. The same 3 old-pipeline tests still fail as before. The rebuilt container is running, and I checked the new section in the browser with your real data. Nothing is committed yet.

**How the limits work**
- **Stop at** (default $90): no AI call is made past this.
- **Ask before spending above** (default $45): past this, every new run has to be confirmed once before it spends. You're at $11.69, so nothing asks yet.
  - When you run a pipeline step in the terminal, it asks `Continue this run? [y/N]`. Answering no stops it before any spending.
  - Setting `BUDGET_CONFIRM=1` confirms a run up front, for unattended runs.
- **The stop is checked first**, so it never asks about a call that would be refused anyway.

**API key**
- A key you save in the app is checked with OpenAI first, using a free call; a rejected key isn't saved.
- It's stored in `data/settings.json`, readable only by your user. It survives snapshot restores and works with the container.
- It takes priority over `.env`. Removing it falls back to `.env`.
- The app never sends the key back; you only ever see `sk-…abcd`.

**Audit:** every change to the key or the limits goes into the audit trail. The key is recorded masked only.

**Rules:** I updated AGENTS rules 12 and 16. The $100 hackathon budget is gone, and agents may not confirm spending or raise a limit on their own; they have to ask you. Logged as D-054, and the hackathon-only "block non-demo jobs at $70" limit is dropped.

1. Remove the dead API routes and their tests. You won't see any difference in the app.
2. Move the helpers the new pipeline still borrows from the old code (audit writer, scoring math, gate prompts) into their new homes.

input.content:
"""The AI agents of the checkpoint pipeline (D-055): one entry per kind of model call, matched by its `llm_usage.job` name.

This is the catalogue the "AI agents" page configures. Each agent keeps the defaults its code passes (tier → model,
reasoning effort); the user's overrides live in `app_settings` ("agents") and `LLM.generate()` / `.embed()` apply them on
every call: model, reasoning effort, on/off, and a spend cap (total committed spend of the agent, enforced by the guard).

Jobs of the earlier wave pipeline (D-022 – D-038) match no agent: they stay in the usage log as history and are not
configurable. Order matters — the first pattern that matches a job wins.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Literal

Kind = Literal["responses", "embeddings"]
Tier = Literal["fast", "smart", "embed"]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Agent:
    key: str
    name: str
    pipeline: str
    description: str
    pattern: str
    kind: Kind = "responses"
    tier: Tier = "fast"
    effort: str | None = "low"   # the reasoning effort its code passes (None for embeddings)
    web_search: bool = False


PIPELINES = [
    ("sources", "Sources", "Web research and price lists: what goes into the evidence."),
    ("structure", "Structure & context", "Comments → signals → clusters → themes → requirement areas (D-043)."),
    ("definition", "Requirement definition", "Areas → requirements with metrics, target ladders and links (D-048)."),
    ("prioritize", "Prioritization", "The fit gate before the deterministic score (D-050)."),
]

AGENTS: list[Agent] = [
    # sources
    Agent("research_web", "Web research agents", "sources",
          "Search the web for competitor, trend, review and market facts; every item cited with URL and quote.",
          r"^research:(?!findings\b|benchmarks\b)", web_search=True),
    Agent("research_findings", "Research summarizer", "sources",
          "Turns cited web items into findings per car line and market.", r"^research:findings\b"),
    Agent("options_reader", "Price-list reader", "sources",
          "Reads BMW's option price lists (PDF pages) into structured options.", r"^ingest:options\b"),
    # structure & context
    Agent("classify", "Comment classifier", "structure",
          "Every customer comment → signals in the shared aspect space (extract-v4).", r"^classify:extract"),
    Agent("context_mapper", "Context mapper", "structure",
          "Maps study items, options and research onto the same aspects as the comments.",
          r"^classify:(study-aspects|option-aspects|research)\b"),
    Agent("standardize", "Insight writer", "structure",
          "Writes one standardized insight per cluster of signals.", r"^contextualize:standardize\b"),
    Agent("duplicates", "Duplicate checker", "structure",
          "Merges insights that say the same thing.", r"^contextualize:duplicates\b"),
    Agent("themes", "Theme namer", "structure", "Names and describes the themes insights group into.",
          r"^contextualize:themes\b"),
    Agent("evidence_linker", "Evidence linker", "structure",
          "Links themes to study, option and research evidence (supports / contradicts / context).",
          r"^contextualize:link\b"),
    Agent("areas", "Area builder", "structure", "Groups themes into potential requirement areas.", r"^areas\b",
          tier="smart", effort="medium"),
    Agent("elicit", "Requirement drafter (areas)", "structure", "Drafts requirements straight from areas (not run yet).",
          r"^elicit\b", tier="smart", effort="medium"),
    Agent("embed_signals", "Signal embeddings", "structure", "Vectors for clustering the signals.",
          r"^embed:signals:v4\b", kind="embeddings", tier="embed", effort=None),
    Agent("embed_context", "Context embeddings", "structure", "Vectors for insights, themes and evidence nodes (RAG).",
          r"^embed:(nodes|insights|themes)\b", kind="embeddings", tier="embed", effort=None),
    Agent("embed_galaxy", "Comment-map embeddings", "structure", "Vectors that lay out the comments in the 3D view.",
          r"^embed:comments:galaxy\b", kind="embeddings", tier="embed", effort=None),
    # requirement definition
    Agent("benchmark_reader", "Benchmark reader", "definition",
